requested_observable_declarations.expectation_basis: Square-planar-derived Ni thiolate cations are normally low-spin doublets; a competitive quartet would require large exchange stabilization from metal-localized d electrons.
requested_observable_declarations.meaning: Electronic-energy gap between the quartet and doublet states of the +1 cation of the trimethylphosphine model, E(quartet) - E(doublet) at relaxed geometries; positive means the doublet (the state expected for EPR) lies lower.

requested_observable_declarations.expectation_basis: Same low-spin expectation as for the PMe3 model; PH3 is a worse donor, which should if anything stabilize the low-spin form further.
requested_observable_declarations.meaning: Electronic-energy gap between the quartet and doublet states of the +1 cation of the workspace PH3 model, E(quartet) - E(doublet) at relaxed geometries; positive means the doublet lies lower.

requested_observable_declarations.expectation_basis: The user's shelf oxidants (Fc+ 0.00 V, acetylferrocenium +0.27 V, tris(4-bromophenyl)aminium +0.70 V) were chosen to bracket the likely couple; Ni(II) bis(thiolate) bis(phosphine) complexes typically oxidize within this window in acetonitrile.
requested_observable_declarations.meaning: Standard one-electron reduction potential of the +/0 couple of the trimethylphosphine model complex, E(Ni+/Ni0), referenced to ferrocenium/ferrocene in acetonitrile at 298.15 K, 1 mol/L standard state.

requested_observable_declarations.expectation_basis: Weaker phosphine donors destabilize the oxidized (cationic) form, so the PH3 model should oxidize at higher (more positive) potential than the PMe3 model; the magnitude of the shift is being measured.
requested_observable_declarations.meaning: Standard one-electron reduction potential of the +/0 couple of the workspace PH3 model complex, E(Ni+/Ni0), referenced to ferrocenium/ferrocene in acetonitrile at 298.15 K, 1 mol/L standard state; PH3 is a far weaker donor than the real ligands.

Atomic spin population on nickel in the doublet cation (electrons), the quantity that distinguishes a nickel(III) (d7, population near 1) from a nickel(II) thiyl-radical description (small population) if the per-atom spin density can be read.
Atomic spin population on the first thiolate sulfur in the doublet cation (electrons); a substantial value on one or both sulfurs indicates thiyl-radical character.
Atomic spin population on the second thiolate sulfur in the doublet cation (electrons).

analysis_nodes.blocked_reason: The declared observables are E(Ni+/Ni0) referenced to ferrocenium/ferrocene in acetonitrile. No ferrocene or ferrocenium geometry artifact exists in this workspace, so G(Fc) and G(Fc+) at the identical level (PBE0-D3BJ/def2-SVP/CPCM-MeCN, 298.15 K, 1 mol/L) cannot be computed; the constants registry offers no Fc scale compatible with CPCM-computed couples, and aqueous SHE absolute-potential constants would cross solvation scales, which cannot defend the requested +/-0.2 V. Required producer: an Fc and Fc+ optimisation pair at the same level starting from a validated ferrocene geometry.

No per-atom spin-population selector resolves on ORCA output in this workspace: the reader exposes Mulliken/Loewdin/Hirshfeld atomic charges only (verified by selector probe on the validated doublet-cation result), so the per-atom spin density these observables require cannot be read from admissible evidence. Required producer: a result whose parser emits per-atom spin populations (e.g. a Gaussian unrestricted output), or a per-atom spin-population selector on an ORCA result.
